Testing your app

Source: vignettes/testing-your-app.Rmd
testing-your-app.Rmd

Authorization needs to be tested together with the application: the package is covered by its own automated tests, but errors more often appear at the seams, for example a forgotten permission check in a handler. This document collects techniques used in the package’s own tests (tests/testthat in its sources) that also suit application tests.

A temporary database

The tests below run on an in-memory SQLite database. If your application runs on MySQL, PostgreSQL, or DuckDB, test on the same database: connect to an empty test schema (its tables may be dropped), and write queries without SQLite-specific functions. An example of running the package’s entire test suite on a chosen database is in dev/run-tests-db.R in its sources.

An in-memory database is enough for the package functions:

new_db <- function(env = parent.frame()) {
  con <- DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), ":memory:")
  withr::defer(if (DBI::dbIsValid(con)) DBI::dbDisconnect(con), envir = env)
  appauth::aa_init_db(con)
  con
}

If the application needs a database file (as the examples do), create tempfile(fileext = ".db"), pass the path through an environment variable or config, and delete the file in withr::defer().

scrypt hashing is intentionally slow (a fraction of a second per password). In a test, create only the users who actually sign in. If a user is needed only as a table row (permission and status checks), insert them with an SQL query:

DBI::dbExecute(
  con, "INSERT INTO users (login, password, role) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
  params = list("ivan", "x", "user")
)

Such a user cannot sign in (the password is not a hash), but is fine for other checks.

Functions without Shiny

User rules, permissions, tokens, and login protection are checked with ordinary expect_*:

test_that("the last administrator cannot be deleted", {
  con <- new_db()
  aa_create_first_admin(con, "boss", "boss-password")
  aa_create_user(con, "ann", "ann-password", "admin")
  aa_delete_user(con, "ann", acting_login = "boss")

  expect_error(
    aa_delete_user(con, "boss", acting_login = "ann"),
    class = "appauth_error_user"
  )
})

test_that("permissions come from the matrix", {
  provider <- aa_permissions_from_matrix(list(Run = c("admin", "user"), Access = "admin"))

  expect_true(aa_can(list(login = "ivan", role = "user"), "Run", provider))
  expect_false(aa_can(list(login = "ivan", role = "user"), "Access", provider))
  expect_false(aa_can(NULL, "Run", provider))      # closed by default
})

Rule errors have the class appauth_error_user and a reason field; the error text is in the language of the settings.

Time for login protection is easiest to set by inserting a record with the needed time. Time is stored as text in UTC (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS), so it is convenient to compute it in R: this way the query is the same for all databases (there is no need for SQL functions like datetime('now'), which exist only in SQLite):

three_minutes_ago <- format(Sys.time() - 180, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", tz = "UTC")

DBI::dbExecute(
  con,
  "INSERT INTO login_attempts (login, success, attempted_at)
   VALUES (?, 0, ?)",
  params = list("ivan", three_minutes_ago)
)
aa_login_lock_remaining(con, "ivan", aa_settings(max_failed_logins = 1))

Modules via testServer

The sign-in, user, and password change modules are tested through shiny::testServer(). It is convenient to wrap the call in a helper, because expr must be passed as an expression:

run_auth <- function(con, expr, settings = aa_settings(), on_event = NULL, ...) {
  rlang::inject(shiny::testServer(
    aa_auth_server,
    args = list(conn = con, settings = settings, on_event = on_event, ...),
    expr = !!rlang::enquo(expr)
  ))
}

test_that("password sign-in", {
  con <- new_db()
  aa_create_user(con, "ivan", "ivan-password", "user")

  run_auth(con, {
    session$setInputs(login = "ivan", password = "wrong", login_btn = 1)
    expect_false(session$returned$logged_in())
    expect_equal(output$message, "Incorrect login or password")

    session$setInputs(login = "ivan", password = "ivan-password", login_btn = 2)
    expect_true(session$returned$logged_in())
    expect_equal(session$returned$user(), list(login = "ivan", role = "user"))
  })
})

For the users module, instead of a real auth an object with a reactive user is enough:

fake_auth <- function(login = "boss", role = "admin") {
  list(user = shiny::reactiveVal(list(login = login, role = role)))
}

Identifiers in a module test have no prefix (login, login_btn); in a whole-application test they carry the module prefix (auth-login, users-open).

Events

The hook collects events into a list, which shows what the package emitted:

events <- list()
hook <- function(event, user, session_id, value) {
  events[[length(events) + 1]] <<- list(event = event, user = user, value = value)
}

Dialog contents

Dialogs are opened through shiny::showModal() and are not visible in testServer. Replace the function and get the HTML the browser would see:

html <- NULL
testthat::local_mocked_bindings(
  showModal = function(ui, ...) html <<- paste(as.character(ui), collapse = ""),
  .package = "shiny"
)

This lets you check that the block button is not shown for oneself, that the card slot is rendered, and that a login containing HTML is escaped.

Time and the guard

In testServer the session time is advanced manually:

shiny::testServer(function(input, output, session) aa_session_guard(auth, con, settings), {
  session$flushReact()
  DBI::dbExecute(con, "UPDATE users SET blocked = 1 WHERE login = 'ivan'")
  session$elapse(35000)               # 35 seconds have passed
  expect_equal(logout_calls[[1]]$reason, "blocked")
})

Whole-application test: load app.R the way runApp() does

shiny::runApp(directory) loads app.R into its own environment, not the global one. If a test runs eval(parse("app.R"), envir = globalenv()), variables created in app.R become global, and an error such as “a function from R/ does not see a variable from app.R” will not reproduce in the test, although in the running application the tab is broken. Load the application into a separate environment:

app_env <- new.env(parent = globalenv())
app_obj <- eval(parse(text = app_code), envir = app_env)
server <- app_env$server

Do not rely only on such tests: load order errors (for example, a file in R/ calls a package function at top level without its own library(appauth), while Shiny sources R/ before app.R) show up only with a real runApp(). Before a release, run the application as in production and open it in a browser. If Rscript in your environment picks up another project’s .Rprofile or R_LIBS_USER, run it with the --no-init-file --no-site-file flags.

Check that the server parts of tabs are registered for those who have the permission: after an administrator signs in, output$access-users-main`` must contain the users table. A test that does not check tab contents under the administrator role will miss an empty tab.

Protecting your application’s handlers

For each action handler, write a “without the permission the handler does not run” test:

test_that("running a task without the permission is rejected", {
  provider <- aa_permissions_from_matrix(list(Run = "admin"))
  auth <- list(user = function() list(login = "olga", role = "viewer"))

  expect_error(
    suppressMessages(aa_require(auth, "Run", provider)),
    class = "shiny.silent.error"
  )
})

In a whole-application test, check that the side effect did not happen (no record added, no task started) and that the hook received access_denied.

Security test checklist for the application

  • Sign-in: wrong password, nonexistent login (same message), empty fields.
  • Lockout after a series of failures; the correct password does not let the user in while locked.
  • A user blocked by the administrator cannot sign in, and their token does not work.
  • Every action handler refuses without the permission (for each role lacking it).
  • A user without the permission does not get the module’s server part.
  • SQL injection in the login and password of the sign-in form does not let anyone in.
  • A login containing HTML and scripts is escaped in all tables and dialogs of the application.
  • The token of a revoked, deleted, or blocked user does not work.
  • An open session ends after blocking, deletion, role change, or password reset.
  • The database connection is closed when the session ends (the database file can be renamed after the sessions stop).

Testing in a real browser

testServer does not test JavaScript: the auto-login cookie, row highlighting, sign-in on Enter. For such checks the package sources include Playwright and Chrome scenarios (dev/e2e): the application starts on a temporary database, the scenario goes through sign-in, blocking, the card, and sign-out, and saves screenshots. They can serve as a basis for your own application. Run such a check on a copy of the database with test users, not on the production database.
